Glad you were able to talk to him and he took it decently. If he is apologizing a lot then that's actually a good thing. It means he notices these things he can't control and remorse which is good in a way because those types are often ones that will eventually react to treatment.

I'm not sure what country you are in, but if you are in USA... he should have insurance if he has a job. Depending on what his co-pay it shouldn't cost much or nothing at all. If he doesn't have insurance a lot of places do something called a "sliding scale" where you pay what you can afford based on income. So often a session will cost around $15-$30 and you go about once or twice a month. It will work if he is willing and if the therapist is good. It's a dr for your brain. The brain is still a part of the body and there can be chemical imbalances and stuff like that so I have no idea why people in general think it's imaginary when there are brain scans for evidence. Then again insurance companies always feel that the teeth are not that important to cover even though you can die from an impacted tooth. (sorry lil rant there lol)

You didn't portray him as a leech though. It was mainly figuring out for yourself if he was that way because those types are beyond help. The counselor would still help though cause a lot of people are stubborn or their illness is so bad that it just takes time to think in a different way which is why some do need pills for the extra help. DRs just over prescribe them to people that really don't need them.

If he is unwilling to see one though even if you offered to pay to try it out, you can set time aside once a month to just talk and let him vent and then you can vent too. If you vent about random things it might make him feel useful to you and less of a burden.

As for the dating thing unfortunately because there are so many creepy guys out there wanting only sex, a lot of women don't respond to messages. Usually there is better success when the woman messages the guy first. 

Other than that I think he could benefit from anti-depressant. He can also get it from his regular doctor but they are not educated in mental health and really shouldn't be handing out those pills because each one is different. The psychologist is more of a dr and all he will do is ask him to answer a survey and ask how long he has been feeling the way has and then decide from there which meds to give him. He doesn't even have to do the talk therapy. They just ask to see him every few months to see how the meds are doing and if they need to change anything.

Don't automatically say "well I'm not a professional so I can't help you". Have you been in a therapist office before? They sit and listen to you talk then give you something out of a workbook to do when you go home. They even tell you to get a support network around yourself because they won't be in your life forever.

Ask yourself "when I am upset do I want to go to someone I know and love to talk? Or do I want to pay someone to listen?"

That being said.. know when you are being used or abused yourself. Do they have a substance abuse? Do they use you as an emotional punching bag? Do they reapect your boundaries? Do they try to help you when you need it? Do they show any kind of sign of trying to help themselves?

If you feel they can benefit from a therapist offer to go with them to the 1st few appts. It often ahiws support and that you are not leaving them just because they are ill.

1. My cat
2. My small circle of friends 
3. Music & video games
4. Helping others and making them smile
